rule: GOAL: Fill the tray to match the top row's color order. CONTROLS: Click a bottom tile to select it, then click a tray slot to place it. RULE: The top row is the target sequence; matching it clears the level. TRAP: The top row is not just a legend; it is the required final arrangement.

GOAL: Guide the yellow marker from the top room into the bottom room by sliding the gray wall. CONTROLS: Click the upper blue block to move the wall right; click the lower blue block to move it left. RULE: The wall shifts as a unit, carrying the player while shrinking one white room and expanding the other. TRAP: Assuming the black bar could be crossed; it is a fixed barrier, forcing movement around its left edge or through the right column.

GOAL: Guide the glowing head to the green gap by feeding white space through the middle corridor. CONTROLS: Click the top junction to widen the middle strip; click the bottom junction to shift the head right. RULE: The head can only move into space that has been pushed through from above, acting like a sliding pipe. TRAP: Clicking the bottom junction without first widening the middle strip wastes actions because the head has nowhere to go.

GOAL: Move the player to the octagon at the top-right. CONTROLS: Click dots to jump along the diagonal line; arrows or other dots do nothing. RULE: Valid moves are diagonal jumps of 2 to 6 spaces in the up-right direction. TRAP: Thinking any distance on the line works; jumps of 1 or more than 6 spaces are rejected.

GOAL: Find the correct third item in the delivery sequence. CONTROLS: Click to select a tile, click a slot to swap, press space to test delivery. RULE: Items are delivered in a fixed order: top-left, top-middle, then a specific bottom slot. TRAP: Assuming the bottom slots were checked left-to-right. The third item was actually in the first bottom slot, not the third.

GOAL: Route four colored tiles from the right edge into matching bins on the left, following a specific sequence. CONTROLS: Click a tile to pick it up, click a slot to place it; press Space to lock in the arrangement. RULE: Tiles must be placed in the order they appear in the bins, reading from left to right. TRAP: Assuming tiles could be placed in any order led to wasted actions; the game checks the sequence strictly.

GOAL: Align each colored bar’s dot with its matching cross marker on the side panels. CONTROLS: Click a bar’s dot to shift it one position toward the panel. RULE: Both dots must land precisely on their respective crosses simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming a single dot alignment would win; only the paired state triggers success.

GOAL: Move the blue token to the marked exit at the far corner. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the token to the next available white tile in that direction. RULE: The token can only land on white tiles, skipping over gaps, while blocked by other colors. TRAP: Assuming you can land on any empty space; only the specific white tiles are valid stops.

GOAL: Arrange seven colored tiles to match a hidden sequence across three trays. CONTROLS: Click tiles to move them between trays; press Space to validate the arrangement. RULE: The sequence reads left-to-right through the top, green, and blue trays in a specific order. TRAP: Assuming the order was simply top-to-bottom caused a mismatch at the third position.

ESTABLISHED: The puzzle is a five-slot combination lock. A white bracket acts as a cursor, currently resting on the fourth slot. FAILED: Moving the cursor with LEFT or RIGHT shifts the bracket along the pink strip but does not change the underlying glyphs. GOAL IS NOT: To match the pink strip to the blue strip by simply selecting the correct position. CONTROLS: LEFT and RIGHT move the white cursor between the five slots. UP and DOWN are untested for changing the selected glyph.

ESTABLISHED: The tail retracts from the right, letting blocks ride on the tip. Green is docked. Budget is tight, roughly fifty moves left. FAILED: Moving green first did not change the dock layout or reveal a new mechanic. GOAL IS NOT: A simple collection task where order is irrelevant or where blocks stack in fixed slots. CONTROLS: UP and DOWN shift the entire snake by six rows. RIGHT extends the tail by six columns. LEFT drags the tip and any attached block back.

ESTABLISHED: Three frames exist. A horizontal bar has three empty slots. Frames can be carried and dropped. FAILED: Tiling the bar with all three frames did not clear the level. The gray block does not fit into the bar. GOAL IS NOT: Simply filling the bar with frames. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the white assembly. SPACE absorbs or drops frames. DOWN/UP rotates the assembly.

GOAL: Arrange seven tiles and a socket into two trays to form a continuous sequence. CONTROLS: Click a tile, then a slot to move it; press space to check the solution. RULE: The socket must sit in the top tray’s middle slot, linking the five top tiles to the three green ones. TRAP: Assuming the socket belongs only in the bottom tray or that the green tray reads independently wastes moves.

ESTABLISHED: The blue bar moves vertically, shifting up to row 12 and down to row 28. It slides horizontally across the left side. The green bar is a shrinking timer, not a playable object. FAILED: Trying to move the blue bar into the yellow cup slots at the bottom. Attempting to push the magenta piece with the blue bar from below. GOAL IS NOT: Landing the blue bar inside the yellow cups. Using the green bar as a physical wall to guide pieces. CONTROLS: UP moves the blue bar one row up. DOWN moves it one row down. RIGHT shifts the bar horizontally to the right.

ESTABLISHED: Slots 1 and 3 consistently redirect the ball right and down respectively. Slot 1’s horizontal bar color does not alter its direction. FAILED: Clicking vertical bars at slots 2, 4, and 5 to set them blue did not produce a clear, distinct movement path in the animation frames. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing the board or reaching a specific corner; the puzzle requires understanding the directional logic of every slot. CONTROLS: Clicking vertical bars toggles their state. Clicking the ball initiates movement through active slots.

GOAL: Align the yellow bracket’s corner tile with the matching color on the ring. CONTROLS: Red and green arrows rotate the ring clockwise or counter-clockwise by one step. RULE: Only the tile under the yellow bracket counts; the rest are distractors. TRAP: Believing the arrows were just labels; they are active buttons that consume moves.

ESTABLISHED: The reference pattern requires purple cells at the four plus positions. The center is currently green, and all other cells are gray. FAILED: Clicking the plus positions once turned them gray. Clicking the center cell did not produce a visible change in the last attempt. GOAL IS NOT: Simply turning all cells green or matching the initial gray state. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell cycles its color. Arrow keys move a cursor or slider on the top bar. The right-edge bar tracks remaining time.

ESTABLISHED: Left and Right move the active cross by three pixels; Space toggles which cross is active. A purple bar tracks a sixty-four step budget. FAILED: Repeatedly shifting the blue cross left without observing any change to the gray dots or boxes. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the cross to a specific coordinate, as dots remain unaffected by arm overlap so far. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the active cross three pixels in that direction; Space switches control between the blue and yellow crosses.

GOAL: Turn all blue tiles red to match the printed legend in the framed grid. CONTROLS: Click a tile to toggle its color between blue and red. RULE: The legend cell in each corner shows exactly which positions must be red. TRAP: Assuming the legend was just decoration; it was the mandatory target pattern for the solution.

GOAL: Guide the sliding piece to the blue head frame. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piece along the track; clicks interact with the grid cells. RULE: The piece moves left along the upper row, bypassing the notched lower section. TRAP: Changing grid colors was a distraction; the piece simply needed to slide left to the target.

ESTABLISHED: Both balls share the same row; moves slide them independently along black segments. FAILED: Repeated UP moves on the left ball stalled; RIGHT moves on the right ball were blocked by segment boundaries. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the top band or making the balls adjacent in the current configuration. CONTROLS: UP/DOWN shift rows by five cells; LEFT/RIGHT shift columns by five cells, applying to both balls simultaneously.

GOAL: Slide the vertical piece up the narrow track to dock with the head. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piece; clicking white grid cells shrinks its width. RULE: The piece must be two blocks wide to fit through the charcoal waist. TRAP: Trying to move up while four blocks wide causes a collision, wasting actions.

ESTABLISHED: The ring center is reachable by placing the purple marker at the midpoint between the cursor and a swapped anchor. FAILED: Moving the white diamond directly to the ring center did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply positioning the white or gray marker near the ring. CONTROLS: Clicking the gray anchor swaps positions with the white cursor; clicking empty space moves the white cursor, generating a purple marker at the midpoint.

ESTABLISHED: The cross is collected. Reaching the neck with the cross is the next step. FAILED: Reaching the neck without the cross. Direct right movement through column 29 is blocked. GOAL IS NOT: Simply touching the neck glyph without the cross item. CONTROLS: RIGHT moves the block five columns east; UP moves it five rows north.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking a green cross picks it up; a gray marker previews a destination two cells away. Clicking that marker places the cross as gray. FAILED: Clicking the purple key did nothing. Random clicks on gray cells without a held piece are wasted steps. GOAL IS NOT: Simply turning all crosses gray. The key’s presence suggests a specific placement or collection mechanic is required. CONTROLS: Click green to hold. Click gray preview to place. Click key to inspect. Use UNDO to revert state changes.

ESTABLISHED: The blue player is a 5x5 block on a black wireframe. A red path connects two red squares, suggesting a route. The goal is a pocket at the bottom right. FAILED: Moving the player down the left bar is blocked by a red square. Rightward movement along the top bar hasn't reached the goal. GOAL IS NOT: A simple slide to the right or down without navigating the red obstacles or path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the 5x5 block along the black wire. SPACE may interact with objects.

ESTABLISHED: White moves freely. Black and purple are static objects. Two distinct frames exist. FAILED: Moving white into the left frame interior did not trigger completion or unlock mechanisms. Clicking black and purple pieces produced no movement or state change. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing white in the left frame. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move white. Mouse clicks inspect or select pieces but do not directly move static objects.

GOAL: Match the framed grid’s tiles to its legend by decoding colors. CONTROLS: Click tiles to toggle blue and red states. RULE: Legend white becomes red; gray becomes blue. TRAP: Assuming all grids were already solved; only the framed one needed fixing.

GOAL: Clear the board by jumping pegs into empty slots until only one remains. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click a highlighted landing spot to jump over an adjacent peg. RULE: Jumps must be orthogonal, landing in an empty space two steps away from the selected peg. TRAP: Assuming diagonal moves were valid wasted time; only straight lines across adjacent pegs work.

GOAL: Move the white marker to the center of the ring. CONTROLS: Clicking a colored point moves the white marker to the midpoint between that point and the gray target. RULE: The white marker always sits exactly halfway between the selected point and the fixed gray endpoint. TRAP: Assuming the marker follows a path or requires complex alignment; simply clicking the ring’s center point directly solved it.

GOAL: Align the white plug’s red feet with the green socket’s prongs by moving the plug left and down. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug horizontally or vertically; SPACE advances the timer or consumes a step. RULE: The plug must fit into the socket’s slot without the red feet extending beyond the green frame’s right edge. TRAP: Believing the red feet should align with the outer edge of the socket rather than the inner prong positions causes overshooting.

GOAL: Route three colored tiles to their matching trays using sockets in the red tray. CONTROLS: Click to move tiles and sockets; Space to submit the final sequence. RULE: Socket color determines the next tray to visit, creating a detour chain. TRAP: Assuming sockets must sit directly above their target trays; they only need to be in the red tray in the correct order.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking the right-side red or blue hat icons moves the corresponding piece in the left grid; other clicks do nothing. FAILED: Clicking individual colored blocks, the dashed line, empty space, or yellow/green dots had no effect. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning pieces in a single column, as the current vertical stack did not clear the level. CONTROLS: Mouse clicks on the right-panel hat icons rotate or reposition the matching left-panel piece.

ESTABLISHED: Yellow tiles sit on the outer ring; brackets are on inner rows. FAILED: Rotating rows directly does not move tiles into the brackets. GOAL IS NOT: Matching bracket colors to adjacent arrow indicators. CONTROLS: Outer green shifts the ring; red and green arrows rotate specific inner rows.

GOAL: Slide the black piece across the mirror line to reach the yellow target spot. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the piece; SPACE attempts to rotate or flip the piece. RULE: Moving the black piece one way makes the gray reflection move the opposite way across the divider. TRAP: Assuming the gray piece was just decoration wasted time; it actually indicates the mirrored position relative to the boundary.

GOAL: Slide the mirrored gray piece onto the yellow target using limited moves. CONTROLS: Arrows move the current active object; SPACE switches between moving the piece and the mirror frame. RULE: Moving the mirror shifts the gray piece opposite to the arrow direction, while moving the piece shifts gray normally. TRAP: Trying to move the piece left directly causes it to hit the board’s edge; you must move the mirror right instead.

ESTABLISHED: The upper-left framed box is the target pattern: white on top, purple on bottom. The canvas currently has purple on top, white on bottom. The stamper rests in a fixed position, covering the middle rows of the canvas. FAILED: Pressing UP and DOWN keys did not move the canvas or the stamper in the current state. Tilted stamping has not yet been tested for reaching lower rows. GOAL IS NOT: All-white or all-purple canvas. The target is specifically a split pattern matching the reference box. ESTABLISHED: The bubble floats upward when touched by rising purple water. The passage to the upper room is at columns 44-48. The bubble starts at column 19 and moves in increments of 5. FAILED: Trying to move the bubble to columns 31 or 36 for alignment, as these positions do not line up with the passage entrance. GOAL IS NOT: To prevent the water from rising or to crush the bubble against the ceiling. The water is a tool for lifting, not an obstacle to avoid. CONTROLS: Left and Right arrows move the bubble horizontally by 5 columns. Up arrow does not move the bubble directly; the water provi

ESTABLISHED: The grid consists of red tiles that toggle to orange when clicked. A specific pattern of fourteen orange tiles is required for completion. FAILED: No clicks have been attempted yet; the previous analysis was purely theoretical mapping of coordinates to tile centers without execution. GOAL IS NOT: The goal is not to keep all tiles red, nor is it to create a random orange pattern. It is a specific, pre-determined configuration. CONTROLS: Clicking a red tile changes it to orange. Clicking an orange tile likely changes it back to red. The timer decreases with each action.

ESTABLISHED: The red tile is a lethal magnet that attacks when the player is within two cells in the same row. Landing on it directly from a safe distance might capture it, but approaching its vicinity triggers a fatal collision. FAILED: Trying to navigate around the red tile by staying in adjacent rows or columns has not provided a clear path to the upper section. GOAL IS NOT: A simple white tile to reach without interaction; the red obstacle is central to the solution. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step; landing on special tiles may trigger effects.

GOAL: Align seven tiles to match bin colors, avoiding the eighth socket. CONTROLS: Click tiles to select, click slots to move, space to verify. RULE: Only the first seven tiles in the read order count; the green socket is ignored if placed last. TRAP: Assuming the green socket acts as a tile in the sequence causes a mismatch at the final bin.

ESTABLISHED: The black bars act as ceilings for the white columns, preventing them from growing above the bar's top edge. FAILED: Attempting to lower a column's top below the adjacent left bar's height results in a no-op. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning columns without respecting the vertical ceiling constraints imposed by the bars. CONTROLS: Clicking a column transfers height to its neighbor, but the destination column cannot rise above the bar to its left.

ESTABLISHED: A purple square must land on the exact center of the upper orange ring. FAILED: Direct placement attempts and simple swaps between the white and gray pieces have not succeeded. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the white piece to any nearby pixel or overlapping the ring's edge. CONTROLS: Clicking a white piece moves it to the selected pixel; clicking a gray piece swaps its position with the white piece.

ESTABLISHED: The piece survives direct contact with red hazards. Green grid cells toggle state on click but do not inherently cause death. FAILED: Moving DOWN from the current position resulted in no movement or death. Clicking non-reference green cells produced no visible effect. GOAL IS NOT: Simply touching the red marker to trigger a win or loss. CONTROLS: Clicking grid cells toggles their color. Arrow keys move the piece. The right-edge white bar decreases with each action, likely representing the remaining budget.

ESTABLISHED: Four yellow feet mark channel openings. Merging one white foot with a yellow foot created gray but did not clear the level. FAILED: Single merges and basic alignment attempts have not solved the puzzle. Budget is depleted. GOAL IS NOT: Simply connecting one pair or reducing block count to ten. CONTROLS: Clicking a plug turns it white, allowing movement via directional inputs. Merging feet destroys one block.

ESTABLISHED: Moves work within eight steps. Merges succeed when clicks sit six steps from both squares. Yellow wins inside the top octagon. FAILED: Nine-step moves are blocked. Clicking too close to one square fails. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the center. The yellow square must fully overlap the octagon. CONTROLS: Click to move or merge. Nearest square responds. Use eight-step limits for safety.

ESTABLISHED: Selecting the rightmost cross and pressing arrow keys produces no movement or state change. FAILED: Using arrow keys to move selected pieces, clicking the yellow cell with a selection, and relying on black corridor cells as landing spots. GOAL IS NOT: A simple jump across the black corridor or a standard edge-wrap mechanic. CONTROLS: Mouse clicks select crosses; arrow keys are currently ineffective on the top board; clicking yellow deselects.

ESTABLISHED: The green bar extends downward to row 50, with the red dot positioned near the bottom, likely at row 49 or 50. The blue bar occupies the right side, starting around column 42. FAILED: Clicking the green-left control multiple times retracted the bar instead of extending it. Previous attempts to align the dot with the blue bar’s edge have not triggered a solution. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the bottom of the screen or overlapping the bars in their current configurations. CONTROLS: Clicking green-left retracts the green bar. Clicking green-right extends it. GOAL: Align the upper piece into the lower socket to form a solid yellow rectangle. CONTROLS: Click slots to toggle movement; blue horizontal with blue vertical moves down, white horizontal moves right. RULE: Five consecutive down moves slide the piece perfectly into the waiting gap. TRAP: Assuming a rightward adjustment was needed wasted time; the pieces were already horizontally aligned.

ESTABLISHED: The black pieces have holes that match the yellow slots' dots, confirming they are the same shape. FAILED: Placing pieces directly into yellow slots without accounting for the mirror reflection leaves the top slots empty. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the black pieces to the yellow shapes on the bottom half of the screen. CONTROLS: Move the black pieces; their gray reflections appear across the horizontal mirror line, which must also land on yellow slots.

GOAL: Align both crosshair arms over each colored dot to collect them all. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active cross; Space switches between the yellow and blue crosses. RULE: A dot is collected only when a cross arm passes directly over its center. TRAP: Believing movement collects dots regardless of alignment; precise positioning is required.
